summary.name: Retrofuturism (Digital and 3D Aesthetics category). Provenance is explicit: the source directly names and describes this visual direction.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: choose one historical period's vision of the future and align objects, instruments, interfaces, type and color to it. Analog controls, early computers and space-age forms are possible directions. Motion should follow that mechanical and display language, not rely only on neon grids.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: depictions of one period's imagined future, including space-age or atomic-age themes. Inferred from combination guidance: invention-focused explainers, museum-style explainers, interactive story worlds and brand experiences about invention. Audience, duration and format: unspecified.
summary.limitations: Explicit: keep one era per piece and never mix incompatible period templates, such as 1950s chrome with 1980s neon grids. Avoid purely decorative dials and pastiche of specific real brands or generic neon synth imagery. Minimum text size and hard duration limits: unspecified.
summary.palette: Scene-dependent: background_policy is scene_dependent, so the example tokens are not approved colors, and no exact task colors are supplied. Examples: background #EEE3CB, foreground #314449, accents #6B9693 and #BC7751, no gradient. Foreground on background measures 8.027:1, while both accents fail body-text contrast (3.121 and 2.871) and serve as decorative fills only. Source frames (seconds 1–8) suggest a darker environment, one neutral hero material and one warm accent reserved for the active state. This is observation, not a fixed rule.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: motion must match the chosen mechanical and display language, and no motion layer is mandatory. Shared guidance favors smooth authored movement, while sharp cuts, impacts and reading holds remain allowed. Video is driven by composition time; scroll or pointer input applies only to interactive delivery. Optional references: motion-012 chapter handoff, motion-015 narrative steps, and motion-039 radial burst, which needs an approved mark or phrase in the scene.
summary.audio: Unspecified: no audio is supplied or mandated for this style. Source-suggested options include restrained mechanical sound accents, ambience, or silence at reading holds, with no fixed genre, tempo or voice. Inferred: silence suits a brief without audio needs. Music synchronization requires inspected audio, and any narration must stay intelligible.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploads are supplied, and the style requires none. Local fonts and assets must load before rendering. Period-appropriate instruments, interfaces or flat background shapes may need to be created or sourced. Motion-039 needs an approved mark or phrase. Source frames are observations, not reusable assets, and no brand marks or copy should be invented.
summary.combinations: Retrofuturism alone suffices when one era defines the whole world. Optional same-era supports: style-075 adds operable analog controls whose switches and dials produce visible state changes; style-009 adds mid-century space-age type and flat background shapes using only primary palette tokens. Do not combine across decades.
summary.productionApproach: Style renderer: Three.js for 3D objects and SVG for flat instruments and interface layers. Motion engine: one paused, seekable GSAP timeline, with Motion used only after synchronization is verified. Pipeline: HyperFrames by default, with Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists. chroma-js validates colors. Verify key frames and the decoded video before delivery.
